_provenance: Hand-maintained by the site maintainer. Each entry records what a project has said in public about its own support for catalog numbers above 99999, with the link and the UTC date of the statement. Nothing in this file was tested by the corpus; the library table is the tested part.

entries.source: Fredy, SatNOGS maintainer, on the Libre Space forum
entries.simple: The open ground-station network. As of 22 September 2026 none of its parts handle satellite numbers above 99,999. Its makers say support for both the lettered numbers and the new OMM format is in progress, and will arrive in stages, one part of the network at a time.
entries.technical: No SatNOGS component supports NORAD ids above 99999 as of 2026-09-22. Support for Alpha-5 and OMM JSON is said to be in progress, with the level of support differing by sub-project. Not tested by the corpus.

entries.source: Alexandru Csete, Gpredict's maintainer, on pull request #412
entries.simple: The free satellite tracker most amateur-radio stations use. The practical position in September 2026: a stock Gpredict fetches CelesTrak's TLE feeds, and CelesTrak leaves every object numbered above 99,999 out of that format, so those satellites are missing from Gpredict rather than misnumbered. If a TLE line with a lettered number does reach it from another source, version 2.6 reads the number as 0 and files the satellite under that number. The maintainer is adding support for CelesTrak's CSV format, which carries the full numbers; that is how these objects would arrive. A July 2026 patch for the lettered numbers was withdrawn by its author, not declined; the maintainer wrote that, as far as he could tell, CelesTrak would not serve the lettered format.
entries.technical: Three facts and a position. (1) If an Alpha-5 line reaches Gpredict 2.6, the catalog field decodes to 0: the parser converts it with atoi (src/sgpsdp/sgp_in.c:117) and the updater with g_ascii_strtod (src/tle-update.c:1001), and both the .sat files and the update hash are keyed by that number. (2) CelesTrak's TLE output omits objects above 99999, so the default feeds in src/sat-cfg.c (gp.php FORMAT=tle) never carry such a line; a stock installation is missing those objects, not corrupting them. (3) The maintainer is adding support for the CelesTrak CSV format (issue #250, open since 2021), which carries the full NORAD_CAT_ID; that is the path by which objects above 99999 would reach Gpredict. Source: PR #412 (2026-07-18) added an Alpha-5 decoder at both sites and was closed the same day by its author as not meant for upstream yet, withdrawn rather than declined; the maintainer's comment of 2026-07-19 says CelesTrak would not, as far as he could tell, support Alpha-5, and that CSV support is in progress.
